speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your chronic cough, can you tell me if you have any shortness of breath, wheezing, or chest pain when you cough?

text: No, I don't experience any shortness of breath, wheezing, or chest pain when I cough. The cough is mostly dry and tends to get worse at night, sometimes disrupting my sleep. speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant finding; bilateral adrenal hyperplasia is indeed a hallmark of Cushing's syndrome. speaker: Patient
text: I have noticed that my face looks a bit rounder lately, and I've been gaining weight in my upper back. My skin seems thinner than usual, and I bruise very easily even from minor bumps. speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cushing's Syndrome (likely ACTH-dependent due to bilateral adrenal hyperplasia). The chronic dry cough is likely secondary to steroid-induced cough hypersensitivity or mild aspiration from potential muscle weakness, though the primary diagnosis is confirmed by your imaging and clinical presentation.
